description: Manual payments and refunds record the acting user (R0-PL-07). Run from apps/server against a migrated isolated database and REDIS_URL, with dist/main.js built for the journey: npx vitest run test/payments-actor.integration.test.ts test/revenue-authorization.integration.test.ts test/release0-journey.integration.test.ts --no-file-parallelism --reporter=json --outputFile=<report>, then node ../../scripts/proof-admission/evaluate.mjs --manifest ../../scripts/proof-admission/manifests/payments-actor.json --report <report>. Required: every payments-actor case, RA-G5-01 and RA-G5-05 (recordedBy is never public), and the three release0-journey step-4 cases that carry the LEDGER claim and have stable titles (one Payment row and one Payment:<id>:payment_recorded posting per payment, a duplicate submit absorbed, the remainder posted). The rest of the journey belongs to release0-journey.json (R0-16), which retitles the step-4 'FIRST FAILING STEP' case and removes the harness recovery case, so this manifest does not bind those titles; requireReportSuccess still rejects the verdict if any case in the report fails. allowAdditionalCases is true for those journey cases and the two pre-existing revenue-authorization it.todo records (RA-G4-13, RA-G16-01). The two R0-11 review gaps PA-17 (ST-R011-2, refunding an unposted payment recorded no refunder) and PA-18 (ST-R011-3, drive-intake approval dropped the approver) are closed by R0-CMF2-PAYMENT-ACTOR-GAPS: their it.todo records are replaced by the required cases PA-17a..PA-17e (every manual refund, posted or not, writes exactly one FINANCE payment_refunded activity row naming the refunder, USER for a person, SYSTEM for KEY, none for a caller with no actor; no ledger row is invented for an unposted payment and Payment.recordedBy keeps the recorder; the row is written with the refund transaction client, so it commits with the refund, a refund that rolls back leaves none and a refused one adds none; the contact-event registry has no refund type, so the audit row is the unified activity row the posted-refund path already wrote) and PA-18a..PA-18b (POST /drive/businesses/:b/intake/:id/approve records the approver as Payment.recordedBy, the posting createdById and the contact event actor, ignoring any recorder named in the plan payload; the ingestion auto-execute, with no human, records null, so PA-08 holds). The R0-CMF2 review repairs add the required cases PA-17f..PA-17g and PA-18c..PA-18d: the refund audit row is no longer handed to the best-effort TimelineService (which swallows every error), so a failing timeline cannot drop it and a refund whose audit insert fails rolls back (500) instead of committing a REFUNDED payment that names nobody (SEC-CMF2-1, CR-CMF2-1); and the drive-intake record_payment step passes idempotencyKey drive:<intakeFileId>:<actionIndex>, so two concurrent approvals of one intake, or a re-run after a crash before the approved flip, record one payment, not two (SEC-CMF2-2). allowAdditionalCases also covers the R0-CMF2 it.todo record PA-18e, fixed only outside that packet's write set: the drive-intake approve route requires no revenue:write, so a revenue:read or crm:read-only STAFF member can record a payment through it (SEC-CMF2-3, needs a module-scope requirement on drive-intake.controller.ts). PA-16 (ST-R011-1, a human PATCH of invoice status PAID attributed to KEY) is closed by R0-CMF1-INVOICE-PATCH-ACTOR: its it.todo is replaced by the required cases PA-16a..PA-16j (PAID, SENT, OVERDUE and VOID through PATCH .../invoices/:id name the human; the body is the whitelisted UpdateInvoiceDto and the service is handed the authenticated user; an invalid status is a 400; a revenue:read member is refused 403 like the dedicated mark-paid route, whose authority PATCH status PAID now requires; the owner's PATCH and mark-paid ledger effects are identical; KEY's flow-executor call and an explicit KEY actor stay attributed to KEY). The R0-CMF1 review repairs add the required cases PA-16k..PA-16m: the service itself refuses a status outside SENT / OVERDUE / VOID / PAID before anything is written, so KEY's commerce_update_invoice can no longer move an invoice to PARTIALLY_PAID, PENDING or FAILED (SEC-CMF1-1); the invoice write routes (PATCH .../invoices/:id, mark-paid, payment-failed, the status route) answer with the contact projected to id, businessId, firstName, lastName and email (SEC-CMF1-2); and KEY's invoice.paid / invoice.sent / invoice.overdue / invoice.void entries are labelled SYSTEM (SEC-CMF1-4). allowAdditionalCases also covers the two R0-CMF1 it.todo records PA-16n and PA-16o, fixed only outside that packet's write set: an omitted actor still means KEY until flow-orchestrator passes KEY explicitly (SEC-CMF1-3), and the ACCRUAL invoice_finalized posting and its void reversal record no creator (SEC-CMF1-5). Until PA-16n and PA-16o are closed, 'the system actor is distinct from a human' is proven only on the paths PA-06, PA-07, PA-14, PA-16a..m, PA-17e and PA-18a..d cover.
